Description: Prostomium truncate, slightly longer than wide, with rudimentary frontal horns (Fig. 6A & B); a pair ofprostomial ridges. Palps extending to setiger 15; 4 rows of papillae proximally and 2 rows distally. Thorax: Parapodiaofsetigers 1-7 similar (Fig. 6C, D), with slender dorsal mediallobes (no. 1), cylindrical postsetal notopodiallaterallamellae (no. 3) and infrasetal ventral neuropodiallobes (no. 6). Setiger 8 (Fig. 6E) with minute dorsal medial lobe (no. 1), cylindrical postsetal notopodial lateral lamellae (no. 3), postsetal ventral neuropodiallobe (no. 8) and digitiform ventral medial lobe (no. 9). Setiger 9 (Fig. 6F) with triangular postsetal notopodial lateral lamella (no. 3), neuropodiallobes similar to those on setiger 8. Thoracic setae bilimbate. Abdomen: Parapodia (Fig. 6G) with small dorsal and ventral medial lobes (nos. 1 & 9), flattened noto- and neuropodial lateral lamellae (nos. 10 & 11). Abdominal setae tridentate hooded hooks (Fig. 6L). Lateral pouches absent. MBW: Dorsally and ventrally blue between setigers 1 and 9 (Fig. 6, H & I). MBA: Dorsally between setigers 3 and 10, lateral blotches on abdomen (Fig. 6,J & K).

MBA: Dorsally between setigers 1 and 9, ventrally between setigers 2 and 9, laterally on abdomen (Fig. 3, K & L).

Thorax: Parapodia similar on setigers 1-8 (Fig. 3D-F), with digitiform dorsal medial lobes (no. 1), cylindrical to somewhat flattened notopodial lateral lamellae (no. 3) and long digitiform infrasetal ventral neuropodiallobes (no. 6). Low presetal and postsetal neuropodiallobes encircle the setae on setiger 8 (Fig. 3F, nos. 7 & 8). Setiger 9 (Fig. 3G) basically as setiger 8, but dorsal medial lobe absent. Thoracic setae limbate. Abdomen: Abdominal parapodia (Fig. 3H) with foliaceous noto- and neuropodial lateral lamellae (nos. 10 & 11), smooth interlamellae present. Abdominal setae tridentate hooded hooks (Fig. 3M). Lateral pouches absent. MBW: Dorsally purple between setigers 1 and 9, ventrally mainly between setigers 4 and 9, purple stripes laterally on abdomen (Fig. 3, I &J). MBA: Dorsally between setigers 1 and 9, ventrally between setigers 2 and 9, laterally on abdomen (Fig. 3, K & L).

Description: Prostomium about as long as wide (Fig. 4A, B), with frontal horns; anterior margin triangular and crenulate. Palps extending to setiger 9 or 10, wIth undefined rows of papillae proximally, 4 rows distally. Thorax: Notopodia ofsetigers 1-8 similar (Fig. 4C-E), gradually increasing in size, triangular dorsal medial lobes fused at the base with foliaceous postsetal notopodiallateral lamellae (nos. 2 & 3). Neuropodia ofsetigers 1-7 with infrasetal ventral neuropodiallobes (Fig. 4C-D, no. 6). Setiger 8 (Fig. 4E) with presetal and postsetal neuropodiallobes (nos. 7 & 8). Setiger 9 (Fig. 4F) with notopodia similar to those of preceding setigers but dorsal medial lobe absent; neuropodia as on setiger 8, but larger postsetal neuropodiallobe (no. 8). Thoracic setae limbate. Abdomen: Abdominal parapodia (Fig. 4G) with small dorsal and ventral medial lobes (nos. 1 & 9), foliaceous noto- and neuropodial lateral lamellae (nos. 10 & 11). Abdominal setae bidentate hooded hooks (Fig. 4L). Lateral pouches absent. MBW: Purple dorsally between setigers 1 and 6, ventrally between setigers 2 and 5 (Fig. 4, H & I). MBA: Dorsal blotches between setigers 4 and 9, dorsolateral blotches ventrally between setigers 6 and 9 (Fig. 4,J & K).

Description: Preserved specimens in alcohol white, irridescent. No colour pattern  along the bod y, except 3 specimens (PMBC no. 4700) pale brown colour occur on branchiae. Prostomium (Fig. 2A) small and rounded; five antennae, ceratophores with many rings and longer than styles (approx. 2:1), anterior lateral antennae, 30 rings, reach back to setiger 3, posterior lateral antennae, 70 rings, reach back to setiger 11, the mediap antennae, 38 rings, reach back to setiger 4; frontal palps (Fig. 2C) filiform as long as tentacular cirri , labial palps (Fig. 2F) rectangular, medially touching, small median fold present between the two labial palps; glandular distal area slightly set off ; lower lips with median section. A median ridge (Fig.2B) present from the peristomium . to the me­ dian antenna ; nuchal grooves along edge of peristomium, grooves separated by the median ridge . Eyes absent. Peristomium (Fig. 2A -B) 2-3 times wider than long; shallow middorsal notch . Tentacular cirri long and slender, inserted distally on pe­ ristomium on each side of notch. Anterior three pairs of parapodia (Fig. 2A) prolonged and diff erent from the following se­ tigers . First setiger (Fig. 3A) with low rounded lobe and long digitiform postsetal lobe. Dorsal and ventral cirri digitiform. A contraction fold present below presetal lobe. The following se­ tigers : smaller but similar to the f irst one; pre­ setal lobes gradually reduced in size; dorsal cirri with small basal swelling from setiger 8 (Fig. 3C); ventral cirri changed into globular ventral glandular pads from setiger 6; more elongated from setiger 7 and succeeding' setigers (Fig. 3B,C). Branchiae from setiger 1-9 with single f ila­ ment only, bifid from setiger 10, reaching a maximum of 6-7 filaments at about setiger 24 and absent about last 50 setigers. First four setigers with tridentate pseudo­ compound hooded  hooks (Fig. 3F). Limbate setae (Fig. 3H) present in all setigers. Pectinate setae (Fig. 3G) occur from setiger 6; each with 13-15 teeth. Bidentate subacicular hooks (Fig. 31) first present from setiger 10. Mandibles (Fig. 20) with calcif ied cutting plates, shaf t slender. Sclerotinized maxillae (Fig. 2E), maxillary formula: Mx I = 1 + 1; Mx II = 7+ 6; Mx Ill = 5 + O; Mx IV = 5 + 11; Mx V =1 + 1. Pygidium with an anal pore and a pair of small anal cirri. Tube with mucous inner layer and outer thin layer of sand grains. The variation encountered within this species was examined by scanning the collected mate" rial and random samples were taken for detailed count. From 19 specimens, the nutnber of rings in anterior lateral antennae avera;ged 26 ± 3 (s.d.), posterior lateral antennae averaged 68 ± 4 (s.d.) and median antenna averaged 38 ± 3 (s.d.).

Description: Maximum length of preserved specimen with 20 chaetigers, 1.43 mm; interparapodial width (middle of the body) about 100 µm, about 160 µm with parapodia; narower in anterior part of the body. Length of smallest specimen (9 chaetigers), 480 µm. Up to 20 chaetigers; mean number of chaetigers in mature specimens with genital chaetae, 18.0 (n = 38). Prostomium perhaps partly retracted into tentacular segment as a result of fixation (see Riser 1990); appearing fused, with separation indistinct. Three bottle-shaped antennae of slightly posterior to lateral ones. Palps completely fused, short, and folded ventrally,with semicircular margin and slight distal notch. Two pairs of pigmented eyes with lenses in rectangular arrangement. Tentacular cirri similar to antennae  but shorter (ca. 35 µm); located at about level of anterior pair of eyes. Nuchal organs difficult to detect as small knobs below the tentacular cirri, a position that may also be due to the assumed retraction of the prostomium. Chaetigerous segments almost homonomous. Dorsal cirri bottle-shaped, but more elongate than antennae and tentacular cirri, and with bases that are less spherical; slightly increasing in length on posterior chaetigers; tips somewhat blunt; as long as or slightly extending beyond chaetigerous lobe. Dorsal cirri absent on chaetiger 2. Chaetigerous lobe with board base; distinct anterior and apical papillae present. Ventral cirri digitiform, directed ventrally, not reaching tip of chaetigerous lobe. Bundles of chaetae with single superior simple cheta, slight curved and tapering  in all parapodia, covered with fine, hairlike serrations subdistally on concave side; 5-7 relatively long bladed heterogomph compound chaetae, with blades regularly serrated, unidentate. Blades of superior most compound chaetae nearly twice as long as inferior ones. Distal parts of shafts with hairlike serrations. Five posterior chaetigers with additional lower simple chaeta with short subdistal serrations, which might not be visible with light microscopy. All chaetigerous lobes with one strong golf club shaped acicula with tip. bent forward almost at a right angle; one needle-like acicula. Papillae on dorsum inconspicuous and difficult to reconize in squash preparations, but visible in cross sections of segments. Parapodial glands in chaetigers 11-14 not obvious. Pygidium with a pair of relatively long (95-110 µm), club-shaped anal cirri resembling dorsal cirri. Pharynx extending from tentacular segment to chaetiger 4 as long as or longer than proventriculus. Margin of pharyngeal opening smooth, with about 10 tiny notches; apex of large paryngeal tooth reaching margin of pharynx. Muscle cells of proventriculus arranged in about 14 transverse rows. Mature specimens with more than 13 chaetigers. Vitellogenic oocyte in chaetigers 11,12, and 13 maturing  independently on either side. Eggs (diameter 107 µm) or embryos attached dorsally on left or right side. Chaetigers 8, 9, and 10 simultaneously with bundles of sperm, forming spherical mass beneath gut in chaetiger 10; details of male genital system in chaetigers 8 and 9 not evident. Mature animals with totally altered parapodia lateroventrally directed in chaetiger 9, with two lobes, posterior one with apical papilla; ventral cirrus absent. Stout putative genital chaeta (length 95 µm) projecting between lobes, straight, with slightly curved apical part and blunt tip, subapically boadened and flattened, tripartite with two longitudinal folds; rows of conspicuous pointed teeth laterally. Compound and simple chaetae lacking; two aciculae still present. Several specimens with chaetigers 14-17 showing different stages of loss of compound and simple chaetae, development of stout putative genital chaeta, and metamorphosis of parapodial lobe. smallest specimens, with 14 chaetigers, having differentiated genital chaeta and altered parapodia in chaetiger 9; largest specimen with unaltered chaetiger 9 possessed 18 chaetigers.
